caption: Sibling fights are rarely about the thing they're fighting about. And sometimes the hardest thing for a kid is to talk about what's really going on with a sibling head-on, so we look for a side door instead. That’s why a show that features siblings, like @gabbysdollhouse, can be exactly that. Watch it together, then say something simple after, low stakes, no lesson attached: “Huh. Sometimes a little sister feels sooo good, and sometimes it can feel sooo hard.” You probably won't get a profound reply. You might get silence. You might get "can I have a snack?" That's okay, I promise it still landed. Because now your kid knows it's okay to feel mad at a sibling, and a feeling that's allowed to exist out loud is a lot less likely to come out sideways later, in a hit, a slammed door, an “I hate you.” Next time you put on a show, if it touches something real in your kid's life, let go of the guilt. You might be doing the most useful parenting of your whole day. #NetflixPartner
